articles.title: FDA's Own Doctor Blew the Whistle on Broken mRNA Vaccine Safety Algorithm — Officials Buried It
articles.summary: US health officials knowingly deployed a flawed safety-signal detection algorithm for mRNA COVID-19 vaccines and then actively suppressed an FDA physician's attempts to fix it. This means adverse event signals may have been systematically missed or minimized during the critical post-authorization surveillance period. The people responsible for protecting the public chose to protect the narrative instead.

articles.title: Health Canada Knew mRNA Vaccines Caused Myocarditis Before Approval — Approved Them Anyway
articles.summary: Documents reveal Health Canada had internal knowledge of myocarditis risks associated with COVID-19 mRNA vaccines prior to granting authorization, yet proceeded without adequate public warning. Young Canadians are now presenting with dramatically elevated rates of heart failure and cardiac injury. This is the definition of regulatory capture: known risk, buried data, and a harmed population.

articles.title: Peter Gøtzsche to HHS: Here Is What Your Vaccine Policy Is Getting Wrong — And What You're Still Hiding
articles.summary: Cochrane co-founder and pharmaceutical industry critic Dr. Peter Gøtzsche submitted formal comments to the US Department of Health and Human Services challenging the scientific integrity of current vaccine policy. Gøtzsche, who was expelled from Cochrane after challenging HPV vaccine safety narratives, is one of the few credentialed voices willing to speak directly to power. His submission names the systemic conflicts of interest that have corrupted vaccine risk-benefit assessments.

articles.title: Capricor Therapeutics Sued for Fabricating Clinical Data to Push Unproven Biologic Through FDA
articles.summary: Capricor Therapeutics faces a securities fraud class action alleging the company made materially false statements about the clinical data underpinning its Biologics License Application for Deramiocel — causing a 64% stock collapse when the truth emerged. This is textbook pharma fraud: manipulated trial integrity sold to investors and regulators alike. The FDA's approval pipeline remains a vector for exactly this kind of deception.

articles.title: Longevity Researcher Outside the System Names the Real Drivers of Chronic Disease — And It Isn't Genetics
articles.summary: Dr. Ahvie Herskowitz, former UCSF clinical professor and founder of Anatara Medicine, lays out a metabolic and mitochondrial framework for chronic disease that the NIH-funded research establishment has systematically ignored in favor of drug-based interventions. His work implicates environmental toxins, gut dysfunction, and metabolic collapse — not genetic bad luck — as the root causes of the epidemic of chronic illness. This is the conversation mainstream medicine refuses to have.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Investors Allege Company Lied About Safety and Efficacy of iLet Diabetes Device
articles.summary: Multiple securities fraud class actions allege that Beta Bionics misled investors and, by extension, regulators and patients about the real-world safety, efficacy, and commercial viability of its iLet automated insulin delivery device — with the stock cratering over 37% when reality broke through. When companies deceive capital markets about medical device performance, patients pay the price in bodies, not dollars. This pattern of hiding safety signals has become standard operating procedure in medtech.

articles.title: Stryker Hid Ongoing Vascular Device Manufacturing Defects from Patients and Investors
articles.summary: Stryker Corporation's CFO admitted that a manufacturing defect causing persistent peripheral vascular problems — previously declared resolved — was never actually fixed, sending shares down nearly 9% in a single session. Patients implanted with defective Stryker vascular devices were never told the problem continued. This is a medical device company choosing stock price management over patient safety disclosure.

articles.title: Hospital Red Flags Ignored for Decades: Serial Killer Nurses Beverley Allitt and Lucy Letby Share the Same Institutional Failure
articles.summary: A father whose infant son was poisoned by nurse Beverley Allitt in 1991 is speaking out after Lucy Letby's convictions revealed that hospital administrators suppressed staff concerns in both cases, separated by over two decades, using near-identical mechanisms of institutional denial. This is not coincidence — it is a systemic pattern of protecting institutional reputation over child lives, with whistleblowers sidelined and warning signs buried by management. Medical institutions have a documented, lethal culture of silence.

articles.title: Pentagon and HHS Open Investigation Into COVID Vaccine Deaths Among Mandated Military Personnel
articles.summary: The Trump administration has launched a formal investigation into whether COVID-19 vaccines contributed to deaths of U.S. service members who were forcibly jabbed under Biden's military vaccine mandate. This is the first official federal acknowledgment that mandatory vaccination of soldiers may have had lethal consequences. If confirmed, it implicates the entire chain of command that silenced dissenting military doctors and discharged troops who refused.

articles.title: Israel Flagged Catastrophic Myocarditis Signal to Global Health Authorities in February 2021 — They Did Nothing
articles.summary: Documented evidence shows Israel was reporting serious myocarditis harm from COVID shots as early as February 2021, and transmitted those warnings to global health authorities. Those authorities buried the signal and continued pushing universal vaccination campaigns, including for young males at highest risk. This is not speculation — it is a documented failure of the post-market surveillance system that cost lives.

articles.title: Capricor Therapeutics Sued for Securities Fraud Over Clinical Data Manipulation — 64% Stock Collapse Exposes the Lie
articles.summary: Capricor Therapeutics faces securities fraud litigation after alleged misrepresentations about clinical data for Deramiocel caused a 64% stock implosion. Investors allege executives made materially false statements about the integrity of data submitted in a Biologics License Application to the FDA. This is exactly the kind of clinical data fraud that never gets prosecuted criminally — only settled quietly after the damage is done.

articles.title: Regeneron Faces Shareholder Fraud Lawsuit — What Were They Hiding for 10 Months?
articles.summary: Investors who acquired Regeneron stock between August 2025 and May 2026 are now plaintiffs in a securities class action alleging material misrepresentations by company executives. The lawsuit covers a ten-month window during which Regeneron's public statements are alleged to have been false or misleading. The pattern mirrors repeated pharma industry behavior: hype the drug, obscure the data, let investors and patients absorb the damage.

articles.title: GLP-1 Drugs Lower Your Inflammation Markers While Quietly Raising Your Risk — And Nobody's Talking About What Happens When You Stop
articles.summary: An independent analysis tears into the GLP-1 drug class — Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro — exposing a dangerous paradox: these drugs may suppress inflammatory biomarkers while driving compensatory physiological changes that create downstream systemic risk. The piece raises the alarm nobody in mainstream medicine will touch: the rebound health crisis waiting for the millions who inevitably discontinue. This is the GLP-1 bubble, and pharma is selling it hard.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Hit With Securities Fraud Class Action After FTC Complaint Exposes Executive Deception
articles.summary: Hims & Hers Health and its executives now face a securities class action after the FTC filed a sweeping federal complaint accusing the company of deceptive practices — allegations executives allegedly knew about and hid from investors. The stock cratered. This is the direct market consequence of a regulatory capture system where companies operate in bad faith for years before any accountability lands. Patients and investors pay the price.

articles.title: Caffeine Activates Ancient Cellular Aging Pathway — Longevity Signal the Drug Industry Can't Patent
articles.summary: Scientists have identified that caffeine activates a conserved cellular energy system tied to stress resistance, DNA repair, and slowed biological aging — a mechanism with profound implications for longevity research. Because caffeine is unpatentable and dirt cheap, expect this line of inquiry to receive minimal pharmaceutical funding and maximum institutional indifference. Independent science is quietly mapping the terrain that industry refuses to fund.

articles.title: Aardvark Therapeutics Executives Sued — Another Biotech Fraud Playing Out in Slow Motion
articles.summary: Pomerantz LLP has filed a class action against Aardvark Therapeutics and its officers, alleging securities violations tied to executive conduct. The lawsuit follows a pattern endemic to small-cap biotech: inflate clinical prospects, attract capital, obscure material risks, collapse. The FDA's priority review apparatus and investor enthusiasm create the perfect environment for this cycle to repeat — and it does, relentlessly, at the expense of sick patients chasing hope.

articles.title: Capricor Therapeutics Sued for Securities Fraud After Concealing Clinical Data That Cratered Stock 64%
articles.summary: Capricor Therapeutics faces a class action lawsuit alleging executives made material misstatements about the integrity of clinical data supporting its Biologics License Application for Deramiocel, causing a 64% stock collapse when reality emerged. This is a textbook case of buried trial data used to prop up a stock price at the expense of patients and investors. The FDA's BLA process — supposed to catch exactly this — apparently did not.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Hit With FTC Lawsuit and Securities Class Action — Telehealth's Dirty Underbelly Exposed
articles.summary: Hims & Hers Health now faces both an FTC federal complaint and a securities class action lawsuit after executives allegedly misled investors about the company's legal exposure. The FTC's sweeping complaint suggests systemic deceptive practices inside one of the most aggressively marketed direct-to-consumer health platforms in America. This is what happens when regulatory capture meets VC-fueled health disruption — patients and investors pay the price.

articles.title: GLP-1 Drugs Lower Your Inflammation Markers While Quietly Raising Your Long-Term Risk — Then You Stop Taking Them
articles.summary: A damning independent analysis reveals that GLP-1 agonists like Ozempic and Wegovy create a paradox: suppressing inflammatory biomarkers in the short term while potentially compounding metabolic debt that comes due when patients inevitably discontinue. The piece names the rebound crisis waiting to unfold at population scale as millions cycle on and off these drugs. This is the story pharma's blockbuster revenue projections cannot afford the public to understand.

articles.title: Caffeine Activates Ancient Cellular Anti-Aging Pathway — A Finding the Supplement Industry Didn't Fund
articles.summary: Scientists have identified that caffeine activates a deep evolutionary cellular energy system linked to stress resistance, DNA repair, and growth regulation — mechanisms directly tied to the biology of aging. The research offers a natural, unpatentable pathway to longevity that major pharmaceutical players have no financial incentive to develop. Notably absent from this discovery: NIH flagship funding or Big Pharma involvement.

articles.title: AI-Designed Drug Shows Biological Age Reversal Across Six Proteomic Clocks — Built Outside the NIH Grant Machine
articles.summary: Insilico Medicine's AI-driven IPF candidate Rentosertib has demonstrated measurable biological age reversal as assessed by six independent proteomic aging clocks, published in Nature Biotechnology. This is the first drug designed entirely by generative AI for an AI-discovered target — developed without the sluggish NIH grant apparatus that has stalled longevity research for decades. The establishment's aging research monopoly is being disrupted from outside.

articles.title: Light as Medicine: The Photobiomodulation Research the Dermatology Industry Doesn't Want Mainstream
articles.summary: An independent analyst makes the case that light exposure — specifically its role in circadian biology, mitochondrial function, and chronic disease reversal — represents one of the most systematically ignored therapeutic modalities in modern medicine. The mechanism is unpatentable, costs nothing, and directly competes with pharmaceutical interventions for metabolic and inflammatory conditions. Decades of supporting research has been sidelined in favor of drug-based protocols that generate revenue.

articles.title: Regeneron Faces Shareholder Class Action — What Did Executives Know and When Did They Hide It?
articles.summary: Robbins Geller has filed a class action against Regeneron Pharmaceuticals covering a 10-month window in which investors allege they were misled about material facts affecting the company's stock price. Regeneron — maker of Dupixent and Eylea — is no stranger to regulatory controversy, and this lawsuit raises fresh questions about what corporate executives disclose to markets versus what they tell regulators. Investors burned; patients left wondering what else wasn't disclosed.

articles.title: Pentagon and HHS Launch Investigation Into COVID Vaccine Deaths Among Mandated Military Personnel
articles.summary: The Trump administration has opened a formal investigation into whether COVID-19 vaccines contributed to deaths of U.S. service members who were forced to take the shots under Biden's military mandate. Soldiers had no informed consent and no legal recourse — and now the bodies may be counted. This is the suppressed safety signal that VAERS critics and military whistleblowers have been screaming about for years.

articles.title: Capricor Therapeutics Sued for Securities Fraud After Hiding Clinical Data — Stock Craters 64%

articles.title: GLP-1 Drugs Are Masking Chronic Inflammation — And the Withdrawal Cliff Is Coming
articles.summary: A deep-dive analysis warns that GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy may simultaneously suppress inflammatory markers while accelerating underlying metabolic dysfunction — creating a dangerous illusion of health. The day patients stop these drugs, the suppressed pathology rebounds with compounding force. The pharmaceutical industry has no financial incentive to fund the long-term discontinuation studies that would prove this.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Executives Face Fraud Suit After FTC Blows Open Deceptive Health Marketing Scheme
articles.summary: The FTC has filed a sweeping federal complaint against Hims & Hers Health, accusing the company of deceptive practices — now compounded by a securities class action against executives who allegedly misled investors about the legal exposure. The telehealth boom built on compounded drugs and direct-to-consumer medical marketing is cracking under regulatory scrutiny. Patients who trusted the platform's health claims are collateral damage.

articles.title: AI Drug Candidate Shows Biological Age Reversal Across Six Proteomic Clocks — Outside the NIH Funding Apparatus
articles.summary: Insilico Medicine's AI-designed IPF drug candidate Rentosertib demonstrated measurable biological age reversal as assessed by six independent proteomic aging clocks, published in Nature Biotechnology. articles.title: Light Therapy as Medicine: The Low-Cost Intervention That Chronic Disease Protocols Systematically Ignore
articles.summary: A detailed analysis argues that specific light exposure — including near-infrared and circadian-aligned sunlight — functions as a potent regulator of mitochondrial function, inflammation, and metabolic disease, yet is systematically absent from clinical guidelines and chronic disease treatment protocols. No pharmaceutical company profits from sunlight. The suppression isn't conspiratorial — it's structural: there is no billing code for photobiomodulation in primary care.
